title: Vim langmap (Dvorak → QWERTY)
description: Remap command keys back to QWERTY physical positions when the OS emulates another layout such as Dvorak. Text input (vim Insert mode, the Ex and search prompts) is left alone.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Master switch. When off, both the vim langmap and the keyboard layout are restored to their defaults.

oneOf.title: Custom — use the langmap setting below

langmap.title: Custom langmap
langmap.description: A vim 'langmap' string, used only when 'preset' is 'custom'. Same format as vim's :set langmap= and VSCodeVim's vim.langmap — comma separated parts, each either a list of from/to character pairs (e.g. `aAbB`) or `fromlist;tolist` (e.g. `abc;ABC`). Escape a literal comma or semicolon with a backslash.

remapCtrl.title: Remap Ctrl combinations
remapCtrl.description: Also apply the langmap to Ctrl/Alt/Meta combinations, so that e.g. Ctrl-d stays on the physical QWERTY 'd' key. Turn this off if your OS level remapper already passes Ctrl combinations through unchanged.

applyToVim.title: Apply to vim command keys
applyToVim.description: Remap keys in vim Normal, Visual and operator-pending modes inside cell editors. Requires jupyterlab-vim.

applyToJupyterShortcuts.title: Apply to JupyterLab shortcuts
applyToJupyterShortcuts.description: Remap JupyterLab's own keybindings — Jupyter Command mode (dd, x, c, v, a, b, z), the command palette and menu mnemonics — by swapping the Lumino keyboard layout. Turn this off if your OS level remapper leaves event.keyCode on the physical key, in which case these shortcuts are already in QWERTY positions.
